entity.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
entity.description: The philosopher who declared God dead and then lost his mind. Became the youngest classics professor in history at 24, wrote his greatest works while sick and nearly blind, then collapsed hugging a beaten horse in Turin. His sister rewrote his legacy to serve the Nazis.

story.name: Friedrich Nietzsche
story.description: Appointed professor at 24 without a doctorate, writes his masterworks in lonely boarding houses across Italy, collapses in a Turin street, and spends 11 years in catatonic silence. Philosophy's most tragic arc.

moments.name: Friedrich Nietzsche Is Born in a Prussian Parsonage
moments.subtitle: Named after the Prussian king who shares his birthday, destined to reject everything his father stood for
moments.description: On October 15, 1844, Friedrich Wilhelm Nietzsche was born in Rocken, a small village near Leipzig in the Prussian Province of Saxony. His father, Carl Ludwig Nietzsche, was a Lutheran pastor, and the boy was named after King Friedrich Wilhelm IV of Prussia, who turned 49 the same day. Nietzsche's father died of a brain disease in 1849 when Friedrich was only four, and his younger brother died six months later. The family moved to Naumburg, where Nietzsche was raised by his mother and aunts. The future destroyer of Christian philosophy grew up in a household steeped in Lutheran piety.

moments.name: A 24-Year-Old Without a Doctorate Becomes a University Professor
moments.subtitle: Basel gives Nietzsche a classics chair before he has even finished his PhD
moments.description: In 1869, Friedrich Nietzsche received an extraordinary offer: a professorship of classical philology at the University of Basel in Switzerland. He was only 24 years old and had neither completed his doctorate nor received a teaching certificate. Leipzig University hastily awarded him an honorary doctorate based on his published philological work. To this day, Nietzsche remains among the youngest tenured classics professors on record. Before moving to Basel, he renounced his Prussian citizenship and remained officially stateless for the rest of his life. The appointment launched a decade of academic work that would give way to his revolutionary philosophy.

moments.name: Nietzsche Writes Thus Spoke Zarathustra in a Rapallo Boarding House
moments.subtitle: Sick, nearly blind, and alone, the philosopher produces his masterwork in ten days
moments.description: In January 1883, Friedrich Nietzsche began writing the first part of Thus Spoke Zarathustra in a small boarding house in Rapallo, a coastal town on the Italian Riviera. Plagued by migraines, near-blindness, and chronic stomach ailments, Nietzsche had resigned from Basel in 1879 and spent years wandering between Swiss and Italian towns seeking relief. He completed Part I in roughly ten days. The book introduced his most famous concepts: the Ubermensch, the eternal recurrence, and the death of God. Despite its later fame as one of the most influential philosophical works ever written, Nietzsche could barely find a publisher willing to print it.

moments.name: Nietzsche Collapses in a Turin Street and Never Recovers
moments.subtitle: The philosopher who questioned all of reality loses his grip on it permanently at age 44
moments.description: On January 3, 1889, Friedrich Nietzsche suffered a complete mental breakdown in Turin, Italy. According to the most well-known account, he witnessed a coachman flogging a horse at the Piazza Carlo Alberto, threw his arms around the animal's neck, and collapsed. He never regained his mental faculties. In the days before his collapse, Nietzsche had been sending bizarre letters signed 'Dionysus' and 'The Crucified' to friends and public figures. He was brought back to Germany and spent his remaining 11 years under the care of his mother and then his sister Elisabeth, who exploited his fame to promote her own nationalist ideology.

moments.name: Nietzsche Dies After 11 Years of Silence in Weimar
moments.subtitle: The most explosive mind in philosophy spent its final decade completely empty
moments.description: On August 25, 1900, Friedrich Nietzsche died in Weimar, Germany, at the age of 55. He had spent the last 11 years of his life in a state of complete mental incapacity following his 1889 breakdown in Turin. During these years, his sister Elisabeth Forster-Nietzsche assumed control of his manuscripts and edited his unpublished writings to align with German ultranationalist ideology, directly contradicting Nietzsche's own explicit opposition to antisemitism and nationalism. The philosopher who had declared 'God is dead' and challenged every certainty of Western thought died unable to recognize his own work.
